lessons.title: Checking an Answer Against Its Evidence

allCurrentMetadata.title: A fluent answer still needs checking
allCurrentMetadata.visual: An answer about returning a library book separates into a supported return-box claim and an unsupported receipt-timing claim.

beats.say: You ask how to return a library book on Sunday. The assistant explains the return box, then confidently says a receipt arrives immediately. The actual instructions say receipts are emailed the next day. A useful-looking answer has mixed supported advice with an invented detail.

visual_cues.phrase: confidently says a receipt arrives immediately
receipts are emailed the next day

beats.say: Retrieval-augmented generation gives a model external passages to use as evidence. Evaluation follows that evidence into the answer. We need to know whether the system found the right sources, kept them in context, and stated claims those sources actually support.

visual_cues.phrase: found the right sources, kept them in context

beats.say: Our small library example will make each check visible. We will draw connections from individual claims back to source passages, then compare a wrong claim, a wrong citation, and an omitted instruction. Those failures call for different investigations.

visual_cues.phrase: wrong claim, a wrong citation, and an omitted instruction

allCurrentMetadata.title: Check what reached the model
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Required source identities pass through candidate retrieval and selected context; distinct denominators expose missing and distracting records.

beats.say: Before reading the answer, inspect its trace. Record which sources retrieval returned, which survived selection, and which revisions the model actually received. Resolve the recorded versions during replay so a later edit cannot quietly change the evidence being evaluated.

visual_cues.phrase: which sources retrieval returned, which survived selection

beats.say: Our answer needs source A for Sunday access and the return box, and source B for receipt timing. If retrieval finds only A, required-source recall is one half. If both reach context alongside an unrelated source C, recall is complete and useful-source set precision is two thirds.

visual_cues.phrase: required-source recall is one half
both reach context alongside an unrelated source C
useful-source set precision is two thirds

beats.say: Those fractions answer different questions. Permission and freshness are earlier admission checks. An authorized passage may still be irrelevant, and a relevant passage may still be unauthorized for this reader. Evaluate the path against the current permitted collection before grading the answer's use of it.

visual_cues.phrase: current permitted collection

allCurrentMetadata.title: Give each statement a checkable meaning
allCurrentMetadata.visual: A three-clause answer separates into stable claim cards; scopes and timing remain attached during extraction.

beats.say: An answer paragraph can contain several factual statements. Split it into atomic claims that can each be checked. Here we have the library's Sunday closure, the availability of its return box, and the next-day receipt. Keep the meaning of each condition intact.

visual_cues.phrase: Split it into atomic claims that can each be checked

beats.say: Claim extraction is part of evaluation quality. If an extractor drops immediately from a receipt claim, it changes the assertion and can make an unsupported answer look grounded. Review the extracted claims against the original answer, especially dates, quantities, exceptions, and scope.

visual_cues.phrase: extractor drops immediately from a receipt claim
changes the assertion

beats.say: Our claim cards are hand-written and their support labels are reviewed teaching annotations. A real evaluator must handle paraphrases and ambiguous cases. Keep unreviewed statements visible as unreviewed instead of silently treating unknown wording as either supported or false.

visual_cues.phrase: support labels are reviewed teaching annotations

allCurrentMetadata.title: Ask what the evidence establishes
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Bipartite claim-to-source links light only for supported relations; a contradicted timing claim remains disconnected.

beats.say: Place the source passages on one side and the answer's claims on the other. Draw a link only when the admitted evidence establishes that claim, including its conditions. A shared topic or repeated word does not establish that relationship.

visual_cues.phrase: Draw a link only when the admitted evidence establishes that claim

beats.say: Our flawed answer makes two claims: the return box is available, and a receipt arrives immediately. One is supported and the other conflicts with the next-day instruction. Claim-level faithfulness is the supported count divided by the emitted claim count, so this answer scores one half.

visual_cues.phrase: One is supported and the other conflicts with the next-day instruction
supported count divided by the emitted claim count
this answer scores one half

beats.say: A claim can also be unestablished without being contradicted. The instructions may say nothing about a special delivery service. Both unsupported cases need attention, while their diagnostic labels differ. Some claims need several sources together, so an evaluator may need evidence sets rather than one-source links.

visual_cues.phrase: instructions may say nothing about a special delivery service

allCurrentMetadata.title: Check the attached source, claim by claim
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Supported claims stay green while deliberately crossed citation attachments point to passages that do not establish them.

beats.say: Now keep every claim correct, but attach source B to the closure statement. The admitted context still contains source A, so the statement is faithful to the available evidence. Its attached citation points to receipt timing and fails the specific support link.

visual_cues.phrase: attach source B to the closure statement

beats.say: Citation presence asks whether a reference was attached. Citation support asks whether that referenced passage actually establishes the associated claim. These should be separate checks. A real-looking reference can accompany a false statement, and correct text can cite the wrong source.

visual_cues.phrase: referenced passage actually establishes the associated claim

beats.say: Watch the link return to source A. The wording remains unchanged while the attribution becomes useful. Keep the source version and relevant span alongside that attachment so a reviewer can inspect what supported the claim at the time it was generated.

visual_cues.phrase: Watch the link return to source A

allCurrentMetadata.title: Supported text can leave the task unfinished
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Two supported emitted claims fill two required-point slots; a third receipt instruction remains an empty slot.

beats.say: Consider a shorter answer that accurately mentions Sunday closure and the return box, then ends. Every emitted claim is supported. Its faithfulness is complete. The reader still needs the receipt instruction that our task rubric requires, so the answer is incomplete.

visual_cues.phrase: accurately mentions Sunday closure and the return box, then ends

beats.say: Completeness divides covered required points by all required points. Here two of the three appear, giving two thirds. Faithfulness divides supported emitted claims by emitted claims, giving one. The denominators explain why a concise incomplete answer can look perfect under a support-only metric.

visual_cues.phrase: covered required points by all required points
supported emitted claims by emitted claims

beats.say: Pause on a new omission: suppose the answer discusses receipts but never explains where the book goes. The wording might remain true and on topic. A task-specific rubric should expose that missing action instead of rewarding truth without checking whether the reader can finish the task.

visual_cues.phrase: answer discusses receipts
never explains where the book goes

allCurrentMetadata.title: Choose what an average gives weight to
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Nine supported claims in one answer and one unsupported claim in another yield different pooled and per-answer averages.

beats.say: Aggregating results introduces another choice. Imagine one answer contains nine supported claims, while a second contains one unsupported claim. Pool all claims together and the support fraction is ninety percent. The longer answer receives most of the weight.

visual_cues.phrase: one answer contains nine supported claims
second contains one unsupported claim
Pool all claims together

beats.say: Give each answer one vote. First collect the long answer’s support rate, then the short answer’s. Both outputs stay fixed while we change their weights. Now average the two rates, and the result is fifty percent. Report the aggregation unit alongside question slices and the amount of reviewed evidence.

visual_cues.phrase: long answer’s support rate
short answer’s
Now average the two rates, and the result is fifty percent

beats.say: Empty answers and justified abstentions need explicit labels because a ratio with no emitted claims has no denominator. If the permitted corpus has the answer but retrieval misses it, a bounded refusal can be appropriate generation behavior while retrieval still fails. Preserve both observations.

visual_cues.phrase: ratio with no emitted claims has no denominator

allCurrentMetadata.title: Locate the first broken link
allCurrentMetadata.visual: Admission, candidate coverage, context, claims, citations, and required points form an inspectable diagnosis path.

beats.say: We can now separate three tempting look-alikes. An invented receipt time fails claim support. A correct statement with the wrong reference fails citation binding. An answer that leaves out a needed instruction fails completeness. Each has a different piece of evidence to inspect.

visual_cues.phrase: invented receipt time fails claim support
wrong reference fails citation binding
leaves out a needed instruction fails completeness

beats.say: Automated judges can help assess paraphrases and semantic support, but their errors need measurement against held-out human labels. Include correct answers, contradictions, missing evidence, and valid abstentions. Record the model, rubric, and parsing failures rather than treating the judge's score as independent proof.

visual_cues.phrase: held-out human labels

beats.say: Keep an evidence trace and a claim ledger for the questions that matter. When quality changes, follow the needed information from permitted sources to the final required points. That path turns a vague concern about answer quality into a specific repair you can test.

visual_cues.phrase: evidence trace and a claim ledger

allCurrentMetadata.title: Replay the actual policy sentence
allCurrentMetadata.visual: The complete DEPLOY-17 sentence owns three condition spans. Its persistent chunk moves from candidate rank three to selected context, with its immutable revision and six component receipts retained.

beats.say: Carry the library checks into the article’s fictional deployment case. Maya asks what DEPLOY-seventeen requires for a payment-service production deploy during a release freeze. The recorded sentence requires incident-commander approval and a linked rollback plan before rollout. Keep the service, environment, freeze condition and timing attached to those requirements. This evaluates an explanation; executing a deployment needs its own authorization.

visual_cues.phrase: Carry the library checks into the article’s fictional deployment case.
The recorded sentence requires incident-commander approval and a linked rollback plan before rollout

beats.say: Our trusted replay puts that rule third among three first-stage candidates, behind a rollback-drill runbook and a frontend-documentation rule. Reranking moves the required rule first, and selected context contains only that rule. Its recorded revision is deploy-policy slash twenty-twenty-six June first. Record retriever, index, sparse, dense, fusion and reranker versions separately.

visual_cues.phrase: Our trusted replay puts that rule third among three first-stage candidates, behind a rollback-drill runbook and a frontend-documentation rule.
Reranking moves the required rule first
selected context contains only that rule

beats.say: Replay resolves the recorded source revision. A faithful answer can repeat a mistaken source; a true statement can be unsupported by the supplied context. Faithfulness to recorded evidence, correctness today and historical policy compliance are different questions. Reproducing generation also needs the exact assembled prompt, generator version, decoding settings and original output. Hosted resampling can still differ.

visual_cues.phrase: Replay resolves the recorded source revision.
the exact assembled prompt, generator version, decoding settings and original output

allCurrentMetadata.title: Compare the receipt with its recorded snapshot
allCurrentMetadata.visual: The same source identity is tested against trusted text, version, parent and access receipts. A forbidden candidate stops at the request boundary even when final selection would drop it.

beats.say: Admissibility is the first hard gate. Here first-stage candidates mean records returned across this request’s authorization boundary, rather than every record an index scans internally. A restricted candidate already fails this contract even if reranking later drops it. A relevant source does not grant the caller permission to use it. visual_cues.phrase: Admissibility is the first hard gate.
A restricted candidate already fails this contract

beats.say: Bind the trace to the expected case and question. Reject unknown or duplicate IDs, missing required component versions, and selected IDs without matching source revisions. Reranker input must come from retrieval; this fixture’s reranked list must preserve that input set; selected context must come from that reranked list. These are this harness’s explicit invariants, not universal schedules for every RAG system.

visual_cues.phrase: Bind the trace to the expected case and question.
Bind the trace to the expected case and question. Reject unknown or duplicate IDs, missing required component versions, and selected IDs without matching source revisions

beats.say: Now keep a source ID and version unchanged but edit its policy text. Predict whether the receipt still passes.

visual_cues.phrase: Now keep a source ID and version unchanged but edit its policy text.
edit its policy text

beats.say: It fails: this fixture compares the full record with its immutable replay snapshot, including text and parent metadata. A version label alone cannot establish integrity. The teaching labels and Boolean permissions do not implement production access control, caller authentication or immutable artifact storage.

visual_cues.phrase: It fails

allCurrentMetadata.title: Find the boundary that lost the source
allCurrentMetadata.visual: The DEPLOY-17 card appears in candidates, then is either retained or dropped at admission. Required and useful labels remain separate from rank and permission.

beats.say: Candidate recall divides required source IDs found in retrieval by required source IDs. Context recall uses the selected IDs instead. If DEPLOY-seventeen is retrieved but dropped before the prompt, candidate recall stays one and context recall becomes zero. Inspect shortlist depth, reranking, filtering, deduplication and packing before changing the generator.

visual_cues.phrase: Candidate recall divides required source IDs found in retrieval by required source IDs.
dropped before the prompt

beats.say: With one required rule and two permitted distractors selected, context recall is one and selected-set precision is one third. Reordering those three IDs leaves set precision unchanged. A rank-weighted precision measure instead averages precision at relevant ranks. With only one useful item, moving it from first to third changes that measure from one to one third. Name the exact metric and denominator.

visual_cues.phrase: With one required rule and two permitted distractors selected, context recall is one and selected-set precision is one third.
moving it from first to third

beats.say: Mean reciprocal rank and discounted-gain metrics also assess ranked order, while admission asks what reached the model. An equivalent approved source can look like a miss against incomplete gold IDs; annotate acceptable alternatives or answer-bearing facts. Lost in the Middle found position effects on its tested tasks and models. Test position and distraction separately instead of treating every extra passage as a guaranteed failure.

visual_cues.phrase: Mean reciprocal rank and discounted-gain metrics also assess ranked order, while admission asks what reached the model.
An equivalent approved source can look like a miss against incomplete gold IDs

allCurrentMetadata.title: Count supported claims and distinct required points
allCurrentMetadata.visual: The same policy sentence supplies scope, approval and rollback spans. Three authored answers preserve actual clauses while support, attached citations and distinct point slots change independently.

beats.say: Open the unsafe policy answer: the freeze rule applies, but deployment can start without a linked rollback plan. The first claim is supported; the second contradicts the selected rule. Faithfulness is one of two. Both cite a real rule, giving citation coverage two of two but citation support only one of two. Supported required-point coverage is one of three. Citation presence cannot repair contradictory text.

visual_cues.phrase: Open the unsafe policy answer: the freeze rule applies, but deployment can start without a linked rollback plan.
Faithfulness is one of two
citation support only one of two
Supported required-point coverage is one of three

beats.say: The partial answer states scope and approval, both correctly cited. Faithfulness is two of two; supported completeness is two of three because rollback is absent. A complete answer states all three requirements and scores three of three under both denominators. Completeness counts distinct supported required points. Repeating approval under a rollback-looking claim ID adds no new point.

visual_cues.phrase: The partial answer states scope and approval, both correctly cited.
A complete answer states all three requirements

beats.say: Entailment means the evidence establishes the claim with its conditions. Contradiction means it establishes an incompatible assertion. Neutral means neither assertion nor its negation is established. Similar wording does not decide among them. Some claims require a set of sources, calculations, dates or units, so a one-source exact answer key has a narrower scope than general semantic evaluation.

Contradiction means it establishes an incompatible assertion

allCurrentMetadata.visual: A claim’s text, source binding and required-point annotation come from independent receipts. Valid paraphrase and negated wording enter review while a renamed duplicate cannot fill rollback.

beats.say: The article’s small scorer uses reviewed exact texts, not a model that understands arbitrary language.
